marks.gloss_en: R' Shimon: three impurities separate from a corpse, two [modes] in each one and the third not in them
R' Shimon: a ladle of grave-dust does not impart impurity by contact; where is its contact? with one of them
R' Shimon: a barley-grain bone imparts impurity by carrying
R' Shimon: a grave cover and wall impart impurity by contact
ודין הוא: He made the weasel impure and the mouse impure -- as the weasel is a species that grows on land, so the mouse is a species that grows on land
since 'mouse' is said, I would hear even a sea mouse, whose name is mouse
או כלך לדרך זו: the analogy runs equally the other way (as 'weasel' is whatever is called weasel, so 'mouse' whatever is called mouse), so the din does not decide; the baraita turns to the verse
או כלך לדרך זו: as 'weasel' is whatever is called weasel, so 'mouse' is whatever is called mouse -- even the sea mouse, whose name is mouse
תלמוד לומר 'על הארץ'
Scripture says 'upon the earth' [excluding the sea mouse]
R' Yehoshua ben Levi, on the first clause: [one who touches the flesh is impure] provided it developed over all of it
whoever teaches it on the first clause -- all the more so on the latter clause
if 'upon the earth' -- one might think: on land it imparts impurity, if it went down to the sea it does not
the egg of a creeping animal in which tissue has formed is pure
'hatteme'im' -- to include the egg and the thigh bone of a creeping animal
the baraita: 'hatteme'im' -- to include the egg of a creeping animal and the thigh bone of a creeping animal
one might think even if [the egg's] tissue has not formed; the verse says 'hasheretz' -- just as a creeping animal has formed tissue, so the egg of a creeping animal whose tissue has formed
one might think even if they were not perforated; the verse says 'one who touches ... shall be impure' -- what can be touched is impure, and what cannot be touched is pure
and how much is its perforation? as a strand of hair
אמר ליה רבי זירא לאביי: אלא מעתה, בהמה בעורה לא תטמא? -- if so, an animal in its hide should not impart impurity
פוק חזי כמה נקבים יש בה -- go out and see how many orifices it has (= p_abaye_nekavim)
Abaye: go out and see how many orifices there are in it [the animal]
אמר ליה רב פפא לרבא: אלא מעתה, כוליא בחלבה לא תטמא? -- if so, a kidney in its fat should not impart impurity
תא חזי כמה חוטין נמשכין הימנה -- come and see how many threads extend from it (= p_rava_chutin)
Rava: come and see how many threads extend from it [the kidney]
the mishna's clause on the thigh bone of a carcass and the thigh bone of a creeping animal, cited by its opening words
the baraita: one might think even if it was perforated; the verse says 'one who touches ... shall be impure' -- what can be touched is impure, and what cannot be touched is pure
Rav Oshaya's dilemma, first side: [a thigh bone] he intended to perforate and did not -- lacking perforation is like lacking an act
Rav Oshaya then resolved it: lacking perforation is not like lacking an act
